## Purpose
#52968 fused the KDA prefill q/k/v conv into AITER's `causal_conv1d_split_qkv_triton_tile_fn` with `block_m=8`, which is slower than the three convs it replaced.
- `block_m=8 -> 128`, bit-identical output.
- `KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder.build` prebuilds the `block_m=128` schedule from `query_start_loc_cpu` (own buffers), so AITER does not fall back to `_build_chunk_schedule` and sync.

## Test Plan
- `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_fused_conv1d.py` (new test: prebuilt schedule matches AITER's, BLOCK_M=8 entry intact, no D2H sync under `set_sync_debug_mode("error")`).
- Kimi-K3 TP8 DCP8 on MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-df6603f0583375f244d1ac6d36265462b7490392`, #63297 on both sides.
- MI325X kernel sweep, same image.

## Test Result
`pytest`: 20 passed on MI355X and MI325X.

**vllm bench serve, MI355X, median per run, avg of 2 seeds** (same image, #63297 on both)

| ISL/OSL, conc | TTFT ms, `block_m=8` | TTFT ms, `block_m=128` | TPOT ms, `block_m=8` | TPOT ms, `block_m=128` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k/1k, c1 | 363 | 359 | 6.29 | 6.27 |
| 8k/1k, c4 | 530 | 531 | 8.41 | 8.42 |
| 64k/1k, c1 | 3059 | 3021 | 6.44 | 6.44 |

**InferenceX agentic c32, 3600 s** (tok/s/GPU): `block_m=8` 14,255, `block_m=128` 14,506. Same image, #63297 on both. The earlier 14,636 was a #52968 revert, not `block_m=128`.

**MI325X kernel, us/call** (dim 1536, prebuilt schedule)

| Tokens | `block_m=8` | `block_m=128` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.50 | 4.27 |
| 256 | 3.53 | 4.56 |
| 512 | 4.55 | 4.61 |
| 2048 | 11.14 | 8.51 |
| 8192 | 41.52 | 26.33 |
| 32 x 8192 | 1605 | 1026 |

Output bit-identical for 8 vs 128 on MI325X.

**Commands

Serve (all arms; `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, InferenceX K3 c32 env):
```
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":320,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[2,4,...,320]}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}' \
  --language-model-only --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 64 --moe-backend auto \
  --quantization-config '{"targets":{"*in_proj_qkvgfab":"fp8_per_channel"}}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":4,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.36}' \
  --stream-interval 10 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --trust-remote-code
```
Agentic: `aiperf profile --url http://localhost:8888 --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --concurrency 32 --benchmark-duration 3600 --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126` (InferenceX `srt_agentic.sh`).

Serve bench: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len {8192,65536} --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency {1,4} --num-prompts {10,40,6} --ignore-eos --seed {11,12}`, after one warmup.

- **Sync**: `KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder.build` now prebuilds the `block_m=128` schedule from `query_start_loc_cpu` with its own buffers; the shared helper is unchanged. New test runs the fused conv under `set_sync_debug_mode("error")`.
- **14,636**: that was the #52968 revert, not `block_m=128`. `block_m=128` is 14,506 vs 14,255 for `block_m=8`, same image, #63297 on both. Commands are in the description.
- **c1 / c4 / 64k**: table in the description, same image on both sides.
- **gfx942**: MI325X kernel sweep in the description; tests pass and output is bit-identical.
- Nit: removed the benchmark comment.

Thanks @hyukjlee , this addresses everything from my review, and CI is green. So LGTM.

For the record, I measured the sync I flagged on an MI325X, using an 8192-token prefill step and one torch thread. The fallback blocks the host until all queued GPU work drains. On a GPU-bound step that costs about 50–100 µs per prefill step. It only gets large (a few ms) when the rest of the step is launch-bound. So the cost is real but small, but the fix is worth keeping.

A few optional cleanups if you want to improve it further. None of them would block the merge for me.

**optional**: _to_device duplicates async_tensor_h2d in vllm/utils/torch_utils.py, which already stages through pinned memory.

**optional**: build_conv1d_chunk_schedule only needs the sequence lengths, since it calls .diff() right away. Passing lengths removes the zeros + cumsum rebuild in build().

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

This can land. `block_m=8` is the regression. At that tile the fused conv is 139 µs a call and 9.88 ms in one prefill step, slower than the three convs it replaced at 4.60 ms. `block_m=128` brings it to 63 µs and 4.43 ms. The existing test already covers 128, including a 1-token sequence.

Thanks a lot for the work! The per-call numbers make a clear case for 128.

One **blocking issue** I see: `compute_causal_conv1d_metadata` only prebuilds the schedule for BLOCK_M=8 (from CPU data, to avoid a sync). With block_m=128, AITER misses nums_dict and falls back to `_build_chunk_schedule`, which does `query_start_loc.diff().to("cpu")` and `.item()`, then copies the result back from unpinned memory. So each prefill step now has a device-to-host sync on the first KDA layer.

Suggestion: could you build the 128 schedule in KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder.build from query_start_loc_cpu instead? Please don't just add 128 to the list in the shared helper: it reuses one batch_ptr / token_chunk_offset_ptr pair across block sizes, so the two entries would alias.

Other comments:

- Is the 14,636 tok/s/GPU number block_m=128 (not a revert of #52968), on the same image as 14,255, with #63297 on both sides? Please add the serve and bench commands.

- Please add TTFT/TPOT at c1 and c4 and one long-ISL point (≥64k), same image on both sides.

- This path also runs on gfx942 so we should check everything is fine there too. An MI325X kernel sweep would cover it.

+def test_prebuilt_block_m_128_schedule(seqlens):
+    """Matches AITER's schedule, keeps the BLOCK_M=8 entry, no D2H sync."""
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    from aiter.ops.triton.gated_delta_net.causal_conv1d_prefill import (
+        _build_chunk_schedule,
+    )
+
+    from vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.kda_metadata import (

+        build_conv1d_chunk_schedule,

+    mixed_qkv, weight, conv_state, cache_indices, qsl, has_initial = _make_inputs(
+        seqlens, has_initial_state=True
+    )
+    proj = mixed_qkv.shape[1] // 3
+    qsl_cpu = qsl.cpu()
+
+    nums_dict, _, _ = compute_causal_conv1d_metadata(qsl_cpu, device=qsl.device)
+    entry_8 = {k: v.clone() for k, v in nums_dict[8].items() if torch.is_tensor(v)}
+    nums_dict[PREFILL_CONV_BLOCK_M] = build_conv1d_chunk_schedule(
+        qsl_cpu, PREFILL_CONV_BLOCK_M, qsl.device
+    )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+
+    tot, batch_ptr, offset_ptr = _build_chunk_schedule(qsl, PREFILL_CONV_BLOCK_M)
+    entry = nums_dict[PREFILL_CONV_BLOCK_M]
+    assert entry["tot"] == tot
+    assert torch.equal(entry["batch_ptr"], batch_ptr)
+    assert torch.equal(entry["token_chunk_offset_ptr"], offset_ptr)
+    for k, v in entry_8.items():
+        assert torch.equal(nums_dict[8][k], v), k
+
+    def run(state, metadata):
+        return fused_fn(
+            mixed_qkv.transpose(0, 1),
+            weight,
+            None,
+            state,
+            qsl,
+            proj,
+            proj,
+            cache_indices=cache_indices,
+            has_initial_state=has_initial,
+            activation="silu",
+            block_m=PREFILL_CONV_BLOCK_M,
+            metadata=metadata,
+            preserve_input_dtype=True,
+        )
+
+    state_ref, state_pre = conv_state.clone(), conv_state.clone()
+    ref = run(state_ref, None)
+    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+    try:
+        out = run(state_pre, SimpleNamespace(nums_dict=nums_dict))
+    finally:
+        torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("default")
+    assert nums_dict[PREFILL_CONV_BLOCK_M] is entry
+    for a, b in zip(out, ref):
+        assert torch.equal(a, b)
+    assert torch.equal(state_pre, state_ref)

+def build_conv1d_chunk_schedule(
+    query_start_loc_cpu: torch.Tensor, block_m: int, device: torch.device
+) -> dict[str, int | torch.Tensor]:
+    """Host-built AITER conv1d chunk schedule: no D2H sync, own buffers."""
+    assert query_start_loc_cpu.device.type == "cpu"
+    nums = (-(-query_start_loc_cpu.diff() // block_m)).to(torch.int64)
+    tot = int(nums.sum())
+    batch_ptr = torch.repeat_interleave(

+    starts = torch.repeat_interleave(nums.cumsum(0) - nums, nums)
+    token_chunk_offset_ptr = (torch.arange(tot, dtype=torch.int64) - starts).to(
+        torch.int32
+    )
+    return {
+        "tot": tot,
+        "batch_ptr": _to_device(batch_ptr, device),
+        "token_chunk_offset_ptr": _to_device(token_chunk_offset_ptr, device),

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

This can land. `block_m=8` is the regression. At that tile the fused conv is 139 µs a call and 9.88 ms in one prefill step, slower than the three convs it replaced at 4.60 ms. `block_m=128` brings it to 63 µs and 4.43 ms. The existing test already covers 128, including a 1-token sequence.

Thanks a lot for the work! The per-call numbers make a clear case for 128.

One **blocking issue** I see: `compute_causal_conv1d_metadata` only prebuilds the schedule for BLOCK_M=8 (from CPU data, to avoid a sync). With block_m=128, AITER misses nums_dict and falls back to `_build_chunk_schedule`, which does `query_start_loc.diff().to("cpu")` and `.item()`, then copies the result back from unpinned memory. So each prefill step now has a device-to-host sync on the first KDA layer.

Suggestion: could you build the 128 schedule in KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder.build from query_start_loc_cpu instead? Please don't just add 128 to the list in the shared helper: it reuses one batch_ptr / token_chunk_offset_ptr pair across block sizes, so the two entries would alias.

Other comments:

- Is the 14,636 tok/s/GPU number block_m=128 (not a revert of #52968), on the same image as 14,255, with #63297 on both sides? Please add the serve and bench commands.

- Please add TTFT/TPOT at c1 and c4 and one long-ISL point (≥64k), same image on both sides.

- This path also runs on gfx942 so we should check everything is fine there too. An MI325X kernel sweep would cover it.
